run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T17:29:24Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained by failed /api/data requests that frontend-proxy proxies to frontend, whose failures are in turn produced by the ad (AdService) dependency becoming unavailable after its container was OOMKilled at 17:28:53Z and restarted at 17:28:54Z. Frontend-proxy error spans were zero through the 2-minute window ending 17:28:24Z and appear in the window ending 17:31:24Z (80 per 2m), matching frontend's GetAds errors, which went from 0 to 81.33 in the same window while successful GetAds spans fell to 0. frontend-proxy's own logs show 500 responses only for GET /api/data ("500 - via_upstream", upstream frontend), while all other routes returned 200/308, so the proxy is relaying an upstream failure rather than originating it. The ad service stopped producing spans after the window ending 17:32:24Z and has produced none since; its pod's readable logs stop at 17:28:50.817Z with nothing from the restarted instance. Deployment ad runs a single replica with limits cpu 50m / memory 450Mi and no probes: the previous container was OOMKilled with exit 137 after reaching ~420MB max usage, and the restarted container is now pinned exactly at its 0.05-core CPU limit with 100% of CFS periods throttled and memory already climbing from 58MB to 378MB in ~11 minutes. Service name resolution, endpoints and node memory are all normal, and no other service shows error spans, so the evidence points to the ad Deployment's resource-constrained single pod as the origin.

claims.text: In the 11-minute window ending 2026-11-16T17:40:00Z, frontend-proxy recorded STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans on both of its operations: ingress 543.77 errors against 6073.89 UNSET spans, and 'router frontend egress' 541.62 errors against 6077.12 UNSET spans.

frontend-proxy's 2-minute error increases were 0 in the windows ending 17:24:24Z and 17:28:24Z, then 80 (window ending 17:31:24Z), 68 (17:34:24Z) and 73.33 (17:37:24Z), identical for the 'ingress' and 'router frontend egress' operations.

frontend-proxy logs between 17:20:00Z and 17:40:38Z show '500 - via_upstream' only for GET /api/data requests (e.g. 'GET /api/data?contextKeys=binoculars HTTP/1.1" 500 - via_upstream'), with the upstream recorded as frontend (service 100.69.24.12:8080), while /api/products, /api/cart, /api/checkout, /api/recommendations and / returned 200 or 308.

In the 11-minute window ending 17:40:00Z frontend's error spans are confined to four related operations at 538.40 each - 'GET', 'GET /api/data', 'executing api route (pages) /api/data' and 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' - plus 'tcp.connect' at 18.27; every other frontend operation shows 0 errors.

frontend's grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds error count went from 0 (window ending 17:28:24Z) to 81.33 (17:31:24Z) to 64 (17:34:24Z) and 68 (17:37:24Z), while successful (UNSET) GetAds spans fell from ~80 per 2m to 5.33 and then to 0, i.e. all ad calls now fail.

The ad service produced ~500-600 UNSET spans per 5 minutes through the window ending 17:30:24Z and 216.7 in the window ending 17:32:24Z, then 0 at 17:34:24Z and 17:37:24Z; over the 11 minutes ending 17:40:00Z ad shows 0 ERROR and 0 UNSET spans, i.e. no server spans at all.

Pod ad-554b849958-fcl25 container 'ad' shows lastState.terminated reason OOMKilled with exitCode 137 at finishedAt 17:28:53Z, current state running startedAt 17:28:54Z, restartCount 1, ready true, limits cpu 50m and memory 450Mi, and no readinessProbe or livenessProbe configured.

Events for ad-554b849958-fcl25 show a second 'Created container: ad' at 17:28:53Z and 'Started container ad' at 17:28:54Z (Pulled/Created/Started each count 2), consistent with the container restart after the OOM kill.

The ad pod's readable logs contain lines only up to 17:28:50.817Z: a fetch restricted to 17:28:40Z-17:40:38Z returned 18 lines all at or before 17:28:50Z, and the wider fetch's newest line is 17:28:50.817405Z, so no request log line exists from the restarted container.
Ad container CPU usage was 0.0040-0.0077 cores before the restart and then 0.0215, 0.0496, 0.0496 and 0.0411 cores, i.e. at the 0.05-core (50m) limit configured in Deployment ad.

CFS throttling ratio for the previous ad container (id a9304b...) was 0.068-0.257, but for the current container (id ed742b...) it is 1.0, 1.0, 0.9988 and 1.0 at 17:29:24Z through 17:38:24Z - every CPU period is throttled.

Ad memory: the previous container's max usage was 420,843,520 bytes and the current container's max usage rose 58,048,512 -> 297,611,264 -> 366,804,992 -> 378,281,984 bytes between 17:29:24Z and 17:38:24Z, still 378,281,984 bytes at 17:40:00Z, against a memory limit of 450Mi (471,859,200 bytes).

Node i-06e4f0f4f681d7e45, which hosts the ad pod, reports MemoryPressure False ('kubelet has sufficient memory available'), DiskPressure False and Ready True, so the OOM kill was not caused by node-level memory pressure.

The ad Service is a ClusterIP on port 8080 -> targetPort 8080 with selector opentelemetry.io/name=ad, and its Endpoints list pod ad-554b849958-fcl25 at 100.96.4.112:8080, so service discovery and selector wiring are intact.

No STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans were recorded in the 11 minutes ending 17:40:00Z for cart, checkout, product-catalog, currency, shipping, email, payment, quote, accounting or image-provider; only frontend (2171.86), frontend-proxy (1085.39), recommendation (1.07) and fraud-detection (1.07) show errors.

recommendation's ~1.03-1.08 errors per 15 minutes were already present in the 15-minute window ending 17:29:24Z, before the alert began, and fraud-detection recorded 0 errors in the two earlier 15-minute windows and 1.06 in the last.

The fraud-detection container was also OOMKilled (exit 137, finished 17:06:25Z, restartCount 1) and its Deployment reports 1 ready replica, a separate earlier restart that did not coincide with the frontend-proxy error onset.
frontend and frontend-proxy CPU throttling ratios were 0.29-0.35 and 0.067-0.106 respectively (no CPU saturation), and the frontend-proxy pod is ready with restartCount 0.

The ad service is not processing requests after its 17:28:54Z restart, and this is the cause of the frontend-proxy alert: ad emits no server spans and no request log lines after 17:28:50Z while frontend's GetAds calls fail at 64-81 per 2 minutes, so the /api/data route fails and frontend-proxy returns 500 'via_upstream' for those requests only.

The OOM kill that started this chain is attributable to the ad container reaching the Deployment's 450Mi memory limit: the pod-cgroup max usage reads exactly 471,859,200 bytes (=450Mi), the previous container's max was 420,843,520 bytes, and the new instance has already grown to 378,281,984 bytes in about 11 minutes.

The restarted ad container's failure to serve is consistent with CPU starvation under Deployment ad's 50m CPU limit: its usage sits exactly at 0.0496 cores and 99.9-100% of CFS periods are throttled from the moment of restart, versus 6-8 millicores and 7-26% throttling beforehand; the container's internal reason for burning its full quota could not be observed directly.

frontend-proxy's failures are not explained by ad service discovery or selector misconfiguration: the ad Service selector opentelemetry.io/name=ad, port 8080 -> 8080, and the Endpoints object resolves to the running pod at 100.96.4.112:8080.

The ongoing GetAds failures are not explained by TCP-level refusal alone: frontend's 'tcp.connect' error spans appear only in the window ending 17:31:24Z (18.27 over 11 minutes, 12 in that window) and are absent afterwards while 64-68 GetAds errors per 2 minutes continue.

frontend-proxy itself was considered as the origin of the errors and rejected: its error spans correspond to '500 - via_upstream' responses only for /api/data (other routes succeed), the recorded upstream is frontend, its pod is ready with restartCount 0, and its CPU throttling is only 6.7-10.6%.

recommendation and fraud-detection error counts were considered as contributors and rejected as the cause of this alert: their rates are about 1 error per 15 minutes, recommendation's is present in the pre-incident window, and neither sits on the failing /api/data -> AdService path.

Review Deployment ad's resource configuration: the 450Mi memory limit was hit (container OOMKilled, exit 137) and the restarted container is pinned at its 50m CPU limit with 100% CFS throttling; raising or right-sizing these limits is the advisory follow-up for the single ad replica.
Add readiness and liveness probes to the ad container: it currently has neither, so a running-but-non-serving container stays in Service endpoints and keeps receiving traffic that fails.

gaps: Jaeger returned no traces newer than 17:04:32Z for the 1-day search, and traces_search for frontend/frontend-proxy over 17:20-17:40Z returned no_data, so error tags and gRPC/HTTP status codes of the incident-time spans could not be read.
The frontend pod produced no readable log lines (0 lines, status read with 0 bytes), so frontend's own error message for /api/data could not be confirmed.
The change_history integration is not available, so when and why Deployment ad's cpu 50m / memory 450Mi limits were set, and whether anything changed at 17:28Z, could not be verified.

The alert rule RequestErrorRate was not returned by the Prometheus rules endpoint (alert-type rule list returned no_data), so the alert expression, threshold and evaluation window are unknown; only the Alertmanager value 1.5333 was supplied.

kube-state-metrics series kube_deployment_status_replicas_* , kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total and rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_count for these services returned no data, so replica-readiness history and gRPC status codes per service were unavailable.

No pod network metrics are available for this cluster, and there is no exec access, so whether requests currently reach the ad container and what the restarted process is doing internally are unknown.
Kubernetes objects and events describe the cluster only at query time (17:41Z-17:43Z); earlier pod states cannot be proven from them.
next_steps: Compare Deployment ad's 450Mi memory limit with the container's growth (58MB to 378MB in ~11 minutes) and the previous instance's ~420MB peak, then decide an appropriate limit/request.
Review the 50m CPU limit on ad given 100% CFS throttling after restart, and consider a CPU-throttling alert for the ad workload.
Add readiness/liveness probes to the ad container so a non-serving instance is removed from the ad Service endpoints.
Collect the current and previous ad container logs directly from node i-06e4f0f4f681d7e45 to learn why the restarted process saturates its CPU quota and writes no request logs.

After any ad pod restart, verify recovery by checking that ad server spans (oteldemo.AdService/GetAds) reappear, frontend's grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds errors return to zero, and frontend-proxy stops logging 500s for /api/data.
